newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish airports not hit by civil service strike.
newsitem.headline: Spanish airports not hit by civil service strike.

text.p: Spanish airports were functioning normally on Wednesday morning, unaffected by a nationwide civil servants strike, the chairman of the airports authority AENA said.
"At 1100 (1000 GMT) 80 percent of flights to and from Madrid's Barajas were on time," Fernando Pina told a news conference.
The delays that occurred were largely because airlines had aircraft and crews in the wrong places after Tuesday night's closure of Madrid's airport due to a fire and subsequent lighting failure.
Only four of 37 programmed flights were delayed at other Spanish airports by mid morning, Pina added.

The 80 percent punctuality rate is considerably better than that achieved at Barajas in recent weeks. In November more than 50 percent of flights were late on an average day. Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44-171-542-7706 Fax+44-171-542-5017
